input: Register for a community first responder program

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Community first responder programs vary widely — some focus on CPR/AED, some on mental health crisis response, some on disaster relief. Knowing the specific type shapes which program to find and what registration involves.
These programs are geographically organized. The user's location determines which specific programs are available to them and which organization runs them.
Whether this is for the user personally or on behalf of a group (e.g., a team at work, a neighborhood group) changes the scale and process of registration.
Many programs require background checks, certifications, physical fitness, or minimum age. Knowing any hard limits the user faces avoids wasted effort on ineligible programs.
The user may already have a specific program in mind or may need help finding one first — this determines whether the first action is searching or directly registering.
Programs differ in time commitment — weekly on-call shifts vs. one-time training events vs. on-demand response. The user's availability and preferred involvement level narrows the right fit.
Success could mean simply submitting a registration form, or it could mean being fully onboarded, trained, and deployed. Knowing the end goal defines when this task is truly complete.

gold.taskTitle: Register for a community first responder program
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to sign up for a community first responder program, which involves finding and completing registration for a local volunteer emergency response initiative.

questions.title: What type of first responder role interests you most?
questions.description: e.g., CPR/cardiac response, mental health crisis, disaster relief, general medical emergency. This determines which program category to target.

questions.title: What city or region are you located in?
questions.description: Community first responder programs are locally organized. The user's location determines which programs and organizations are available.

questions.title: Are you registering just yourself or a group?
questions.description: Individual sign-up vs. group enrollment (e.g., a workplace team or neighborhood watch) involves different registration processes and volumes.

questions.title: Do you have any existing certifications like CPR or first aid?
questions.description: Some programs require prerequisites; others provide full training from scratch. Knowing current qualifications avoids programs the user isn't yet eligible for.

questions.title: Do you already have a specific program in mind?
questions.description: If the user has already identified a program, the next step is direct registration. If not, the first step is researching and shortlisting options.

questions.title: How much time can you commit on an ongoing basis?
questions.description: Programs range from occasional training days to regular on-call shifts. Availability determines which programs are a realistic fit.

questions.title: What does success look like at the end of this process?
questions.description: e.g., just submitting the registration form, receiving a confirmation, completing orientation, or being fully trained and deployed as an active responder.
